title: This is Fonseca's teaching
source_text: XXXI. Haec inter alios est Fonsecae doctrina. Statuit enim. Ante omnem praescientiam actuum liberorum, nullos eorum ab aeterno esse praedefinitos: quia alioqui tolleretur libertas voluntatis creatae: sed post praescientiam futurorum actuum liberorum in statu conditionato, bonos tantum a Deo esse praedefinitos, quia eos solum approbat; etsi autem mali non sint praedefiniti; esse tamen praedefinitam eorum permissionem, quam Deus approbat. In 6. Metaph. cap. 2. quaest. 5. sect. 7.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. This among others is the doctrine of Fonseca. For he lays down. Before all foreknowledge of free acts, none of them have been predefined from eternity: because otherwise the freedom of the created will would be taken away: but after the foreknowledge of future free acts in the conditioned state, only the good have been predefined by God, because he approves them alone; but although the evil are not predefined; yet their permission has been predefined, which God approves. On 6 Metaph. chap. 2, quest. 5, sect. 7.
pass_b_english: Fonseca, among others, teaches this. He holds that before any foreknowledge of free acts, none of them were predefined from eternity, since otherwise the freedom of the created will would be removed.

After God foreknew future free acts in the conditional state, only the good ones were predefined by him, because only they have his approval. Evil acts are not predefined, but their permission, which God approves, has been predefined. Commentary on Metaphysics 6, chapter 2, question 5, section 7.

lemmas.gloss: Before all foreknowledge of free acts
yet their permission has been predefined

choices.why: God's fixing an act beforehand by decree; 'predefine' keeps the Schools' term distinct from predetermination, and 'foreordain' renders praefinire where the authors use it as a synonym.
